That's not really a bug, the POT generator is rather limited currently. There is a proposal that would cover this: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10139

The only workaround for now is either using the hard-coded extractable variable names or adding a custom format and EditorTranslationParserPlugin.

Also found this issue today, according to #89286 and the source code at `packed_scene_translation_parser_plugin.cpp`:
 https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/fe6f78a4c788e6a9fddb333d1cb467ee572262e8/editor/translations/packed_scene_translation_parser_plugin.cpp#L224-L239

naming the class member as `*_text` would be a quick way of solving this.

Example here. This is a little hack without refactoring existing class member, and makes the string for extracting visible in the inspector:

```gdscript
class_name SettingWidgetRow

## Having a member called [code]label_text[/code],
##  but not saved in tscn as node.
@export var param: SettingWidgetParam

## Since it is strange to redeclare a [code]label_text[/code] in this class again.
@export_custom(
    PropertyHint.PROPERTY_HINT_NONE, "",
    PropertyUsageFlags.PROPERTY_USAGE_EDITOR
    | PropertyUsageFlags.PROPERTY_USAGE_STORAGE
    | PropertyUsageFlags.PROPERTY_USAGE_READ_ONLY
)
var generated_label_text: String:
    set(ignore_value):
        pass
    get():
        if self.param != null and Engine.is_editor_hint() and self.is_node_ready():
            return self.param.label_text
        else:
            return ""
```

PS: found this solution also being discussed here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10139#issuecomment-3598615746

Hi all. I have read some related issue/PR about POT generation. Thanks for the recent workaround, especially #108909 (`_customize_strings`), which is a useful and powerful solution for picking essential strings to generate translation in post-processing.

However, as discussed in godotengine/godot-proposals#10139 (`@export_translation`), the core iisue of this issue still remains: exported properties does not have a user-specified markers of "this member should be extracted to POT". #89286 (extract POT by `lookup_properties`) is a hard-coded solution capturing many use cases, however, as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/89286#pullrequestreview-1925413379 comments, it might over-collect unwanted strings, or let users to use a name-hack for a quicker way of fixing (as I commented above).

Would maintainers be open to a **marker-based, more built-in approach** (e.g. `@export_translation`, or a dedicated hint/usage flag for `@export_custom`), so the POT generator can extract only explicitly marked exported Strings / arrays ? This approach enables users to directly define the behaviour along with the class member definition, rather than defining in a separated file or a hard-coded string.

If this direction is acceptable, I can work on a PR, and add an options in *Project Settings* first (default off). Just want to confirm the preferred design path before implementing.

The current code for extracting translations from scenes would require some changes to support custom annotations, as it doesn't have any context about property definitions. But yeah, that would be a nice solution.
It can also be considered for built-in properties, but some of them have more advanced parsing logic, so the text can't be extracted universally as is. (which might also be a problem in case of user properties)
